tip: When ordering, the number usually follows the dish: nasi goreng satu – literally 'fried rice, one'.
Itu comes after its noun: toko itu = that shop, literally 'shop that'. Ini (this) follows its noun the same way.
Belum means not yet: pesanan saya belum datang. Use belum, not tidak, for anything that could still happen.
Kami means we/our but excludes the person you're talking to: pesanan kami = our order, not yours. Kita would include them.
Sekali means very but comes after the adjective: enak sekali = very tasty, literally 'tasty very'.
